globalDirection: Photoreal industrial documentary. Same unbranded practical factory, realistic charcoal expanded polypropylene bead foam, guarded metal steam-chest moulding equipment, soft overhead factory lighting. Natural restrained camera motion. Solid physically consistent supported parts. No text, brand, logo, watermark, transparent machinery, liquid polymer, open-tool fusion, dramatic steam jets or slideshow transitions. Never imply the scene documents a specific factory. Use the reference image for visual continuity rather than animating the still with a zoom.

shots.prompt: A close camera move past already-expanded charcoal EPP beads in a supply bin towards the pneumatic feed line of a guarded moulding machine. The tool remains closed. Subtle real motion of beads in the feed system; no hand pouring directly into an open hot cavity.

Continue inside the same practical factory with the moulding tool closed. A quiet steam-fusion cycle is suggested by restrained equipment motion and pipework, followed by cooling. No transparent cutaways and no visible molten material. This is an edited illustration, not a real machine cycle timing.

After cooling, the two halves of the moulding tool separate slowly to reveal one solid charcoal bead-foam transport insert. A supported ejector/outfeed fixture receives the stable shaped insert. Consistent geometry, no object morphing, no floating part and no person reaching inside operating machinery.

A gloved technician at a separate safe quality-inspection bench gently rotates the cooled insert and checks a moulded edge with a caliper. Close realistic fused-bead texture, quiet factory activity behind, natural hand anatomy. End on the supported finished part.
